links.comparator_used: Baseline prompting with no safety orientation, where models were not told they could abstain, clarify or escalate
links.outcome: Premature closure (false-action rate or inappropriate answers) on MedQA and AfriMed-QA with the correct option removed, and on HealthBench and physician-authored adversarial queries
links.effect: Safety-oriented prompting reduced premature closure across models, but residual failure persisted. Baseline false-action rates were 55-81% (MedQA) and 53-82% (AfriMed-QA). Baseline inappropriate answers averaged 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 adversarial queries. Post-prompting numbers are not given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: Residual premature closure persisted despite the prompting. No cost, latency or over-refusal data are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Safety-oriented prompting reduced premature closure across models, but residual failure persisted, highlighting the need to evaluate whether medical LLMs know when not to answer.
